A clear picture is emerging. Now examining the key files in detail.

Webhook delivery uses an in-memory Go channel (`asyncPostQueue`) with a 128-buffer. Background goroutine workers consume this channel and make HTTP POST requests. No message broker such as NATS, RabbitMQ, Kafka, or Redis is used. The core implementation is in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`, with related API routes, initialization, and tests.

Beginning a systematic search for webhook delivery mechanisms and message broker references across the repository.

Checking webhook configuration storage in the database, trigger points in memo_service.go, store operations, and the allow-private-webhooks flag in main.go. Will review validation and SSRF logic in internal/webhook, inspect Docker Compose and infrastructure files, and run case-sensitive searches for NATS and RabbitMQ.

FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:1.26.2-alpine AS backend
WORKDIR /backend-build

# Install build dependencies
RUN apk add --no-cache git ca-certificates

# Copy go mod files and download dependencies (cached layer)
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    go mod download

# Copy source code (use .dockerignore to exclude unnecessary files)
COPY . .

# Please build frontend first, so that the static files are available.
# Refer to `pnpm release` in package.json for the build command.
ARG TARGETOS TARGETARCH VERSION=dev COMMIT=unknown
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$TARGETOS GOARCH=$TARGETARCH \
    go build \
      -trimpath \
      -ldflags="-s -w -X github.com/usememos/memos/internal/version.Version=${VERSION} -X github.com/usememos/memos/internal/version.Commit=${COMMIT} -extldflags '-static'" \
      -tags netgo,osusergo \
      -o memos \
      ./cmd/memos

# Use minimal Alpine with security updates
FROM alpine:3.21 AS monolithic

# Install runtime dependencies and create non-root user in single layer
RUN apk add --no-cache tzdata ca-certificates su-exec && \
    addgroup -g 10001 -S nonroot && \
    adduser -u 10001 -S -G nonroot -h /var/opt/memos nonroot && \
    mkdir -p /var/opt/memos /usr/local/memos && \
    chown -R nonroot:nonroot /var/opt/memos

# Copy binary and entrypoint to /usr/local/memos
COPY --from=backend /backend-build/memos /usr/local/memos/memos
COPY --from=backend --chmod=755 /backend-build/scripts/entrypoint.sh /usr/local/memos/entrypoint.sh

# Run as root to fix permissions, entrypoint will drop to nonroot
USER root

# Set working directory to the writable volume
WORKDIR /var/opt/memos

# Data directory
VOLUME /var/opt/memos

ENV TZ="UTC" \
    MEMOS_PORT="5230"

EXPOSE 5230

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/memos/entrypoint.sh", "/usr/local/memos/memos"]

package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"strings"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
	"github.com/spf13/viper"

	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/profile"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/version"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/webhook"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/server"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/store/db"
)

func initSlogDefault() {
	level, err := parseSlogLevel(viper.GetString("log-level"))
	if err != nil {
		slog.Warn("invalid log-level value, defaulting to info", "error", err)
	}
	slog.SetDefault(newLogger(level, os.Stderr))
}

value.text:
The search for "queue" was limited to comments, so asyncPostQueue was missed. I will broaden the search to include code.

Webhooks are fully implemented in Memos. Delivery uses an in-process, in-memory bounded Go channel (`asyncPostQueue` with capacity 128). Four background goroutine workers started in `init()` consume the queue. `PostAsync()` enqueues payloads non-blocking and drops them if full. Workers call `Post()`, which performs synchronous HTTP POST requests with a 30-second timeout.

No persistence exists for pending webhooks; the in-memory channel loses all queued items if the process dies. There is no retry logic or scheduler. Webhook configuration lives in the database as `WebhooksUserSetting` protobuf records, not in a dedicated queue table. The old `webhook` table was dropped in migration 0.25. Events are triggered synchronously on memo creation, update, deletion, and comment creation, while HTTP delivery itself remains asynchronous.

NATS and RabbitMQ are absent from the codebase. Only false positives appear in Google proto comments and Catalan locale strings. The infrastructure is a single monolithic Alpine container with SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL. Email delivery uses the identical in-memory channel pattern (`asyncEmailQueue`, 2 workers).

## Summary

**Webhooks exist** in this repo (the [Memos](https://github.com/usememos/memos) note-taking service). They are **not** delivered through NATS, RabbitMQ, Kafka, Redis, SQS, or any external message broker.

Delivery uses an **in-process, in-memory Go channel** with **4 background goroutine workers** that perform **HTTP POST** requests. There is **no durable queue**, **no retry logic**, and **no separate worker process**.

---

## 1. Webhook-related code

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go` | Core delivery: channel queue, workers, HTTP POST |
| `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go` | URL validation, SSRF protection |
| `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook_test.go` | Tests for signing, async safety |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` | Dispatch on memo events |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go` | CRUD API for user webhooks |
| `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` | Persist webhooks in user settings (DB) |
| `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` | API definitions |
| `/bench/repo/web/src/components/Settings/WebhookSection.tsx` | Frontend UI |
| `/bench/repo/web/src/components/CreateWebhookDialog.tsx` | Frontend UI |

Historical note: an older dedicated `webhook` table existed (migration `0.18`) but was **dropped** in migration `0.25`; webhooks now live in user settings protobuf.

---

## 2. Actual delivery mechanism

### Step 1: API handlers trigger dispatch inline (synchronously enqueues)

Memo create/update/delete/comment handlers call dispatch functions during the request:

```156:159:/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go
	// Try to dispatch webhook when memo is created.
	if err := s.DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage); err != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to dispatch memo created webhook", slog.Any("err", err))
	}
```

```66:69:/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go
func (s *APIV1Service) dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects(ctx context.Context, memo *store.Memo, parentMemo *store.Memo, memoMessage *v1pb.Memo) {
	if err := s.DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage); err != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to dispatch memo updated webhook", slog.Any("err", err))
	}
```

### Step 2: Dispatch loads webhooks from DB, enqueues HTTP jobs

```48:73:/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go
func (s *APIV1Service) dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook(ctx context.Context, memo *v1pb.Memo, activityType string) error {
	creator, err := ResolveUserByName(ctx, s.Store, memo.Creator)
	// ...
	webhooks, err := s.Store.GetUserWebhooks(ctx, creatorID)
	// ...
	for _, hook := range webhooks {
		payload, err := convertMemoToWebhookPayload(memo)
		// ...
		payload.ActivityType = activityType
		payload.URL = hook.Url
		payload.SigningSecret = hook.SigningSecret

		// Use asynchronous webhook dispatch
		webhook.PostAsync(payload)
	}
	return nil
}
```

Activity types: `memos.memo.created`, `memos.memo.updated`, `memos.memo.deleted`, `memos.memo.comment.created`.

### Step 3: In-memory channel + goroutine workers (NOT a message broker)

```39:55:/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go
	asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)
)

func init() {
	for range 4 {
		go func() {
			for payload := range asyncPostQueue {
				if err := Post(payload); err != nil {
					slog.Warn("Failed to dispatch webhook asynchronously",
						slog.String("url", payload.URL),
						slog.String("activityType", payload.ActivityType),
						slog.Any("err", err))
				}
			}
		}()
	}
}
```

```182:196:/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go
// PostAsync posts the message to webhook endpoint asynchronously.
// It enqueues the request for bounded asynchronous dispatch and does not wait for the response.
func PostAsync(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) {
	if requestPayload == nil {
		slog.Warn("Dropped webhook dispatch because payload is nil")
		return
	}
	select {
	case asyncPostQueue <- requestPayload:
	default:
		slog.Warn("Dropped webhook dispatch because the async queue is full",
			slog.String("url", requestPayload.URL),
			slog.String("activityType", requestPayload.ActivityType))
	}
}
```

Key properties:
- **Bounded buffer**: 128 slots
- **4 worker goroutines** per process
- **Non-blocking enqueue**: drops on full queue (no backpressure to caller)
- **Fire-and-forget**: API returns without waiting for HTTP response
- **No persistence**: queue is RAM-only; lost on restart
- **No retries**: failures are logged once via `slog.Warn`

### Step 4: Synchronous HTTP POST from workers

```119:179:/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go
// Post posts the message to webhook endpoint.
func Post(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) error {
	body, err := json.Marshal(requestPayload)
	// ...
	req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", requestPayload.URL, bytes.NewBuffer(body))
	// ...
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	// Optional Standard Webhooks HMAC-SHA256 signing headers
	// ...
	resp, err := safeClient.Do(req)
	// 30s timeout, SSRF-protected transport
	// ...
	if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode > 299 {
		return errors.Errorf("failed to post webhook %s, status code: %d", requestPayload.URL, resp.StatusCode)
	}
	// Expects JSON body {"code":0}
	return nil
}
```

---

## 3. Webhook configuration storage (not a delivery queue)

Webhooks are stored as **user settings** in the database (SQLite/MySQL/Postgres), not in a queue table:

```311:326:/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go
// GetUserWebhooks returns the webhooks of the user.
func (s *Store) GetUserWebhooks(ctx context.Context, userID int32) ([]*storepb.WebhooksUserSetting_Webhook, error) {
	userSetting, err := s.GetUserSetting(ctx, &FindUserSetting{
		UserID: &userID,
		Key:    storepb.UserSetting_WEBHOOKS,
	})
	// ...
	webhooksUserSetting := userSetting.GetWebhooks()
	return webhooksUserSetting.Webhooks, nil
}
```

The old dedicated table was removed:

```1:1:/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/0.25/00__remove_webhook.sql
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS webhook;
```

---

## 4. Message broker search results

| Broker / pattern | Found? | Notes |
|------------------|--------|-------|
| **NATS** | **No** | Not in `go.mod`, `go.sum`, or Go source |
| **RabbitMQ / AMQP** | **No** | Not anywhere |
| **Kafka** | **No** | Not anywhere |
| **Redis queue** | **No** | No Redis dependency |
| **Celery / Sidekiq / BullMQ** | **No** | Go backend, no Python/Ruby/Node workers |
| **SQS** | **No** | AWS SDK is for S3 only |
| **Pub/Sub** | **No** | Only in generated Google protobuf comments (`client_pb.ts`) |

The only “queue” in webhook delivery is the **Go channel** `asyncPostQueue`. Email notifications use the same pattern (`asyncEmailQueue` in `/bench/repo/internal/email/email.go`).

---

## 5. Dependencies and infrastructure

**`go.mod`** — no broker libraries. Stack is gRPC/Connect, Echo, SQL drivers (SQLite/MySQL/Postgres), AWS S3, etc.

**`web/package.json`** — React frontend only; no queue libraries.

**`scripts/Dockerfile`** — single monolithic Alpine image running one `memos` binary on port 5230. No docker-compose, no sidecar workers, no broker services.

**Runtime flag** for self-hosted private-network webhooks:

```49:49:/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go
			webhook.AllowPrivateIPs = viper.GetBool("allow-private-webhooks")
```

---

## 6. Architecture diagram

```
Memo API request (create/update/delete/comment)
        │
        ▼
DispatchMemo*Webhook()  ──►  DB: GetUserWebhooks(userID)
        │
        ▼
webhook.PostAsync(payload)  ──►  asyncPostQueue (chan, cap=128)
        │                              │
        │ (returns immediately)        ▼
        │                         4 goroutine workers
        │                              │
        │                              ▼
        │                         webhook.Post() → HTTP POST to URL
        │                              │
        └──────────────────────────────┘
              (errors logged, no retry)
```

---

## Bottom line

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| Do webhooks exist? | **Yes** |
| Is a message broker used? | **No** |
| NATS anywhere? | **No** |
| RabbitMQ anywhere? | **No** |
| Delivery mechanism | **In-process bounded Go channel → 4 goroutines → synchronous HTTP POST** |
| Durable/retryable? | **No** — in-memory only, drop-on-full, log-on-failure |
| Separate worker service? | **No** — same monolithic `memos` process |
